items.title: Live: Delta Goodrem takes fourth spot in Eurovision 2026 as Bulgaria wins
items.description: Delta Goodrem’s vocals kept Australia among the favourites during the vote count, securing a fourth-place finish. Follow live.

items.title: Aspiration has changed since the Howard era. This budget is finally catching up
items.description: At the turn of the century, "aspiration" described Australians who wanted to put their kids into private school and university, and to build their wealth by getting an investment property or two. Today, it means something humbler; millions of younger Australians simply aspire to own a home one day, to have some shelter.

items.title: Why some Australian homebuyers are turning to Islamic financing
items.description: When Wildan decided to buy a property he didn't even consider a conventional loan. Instead, he opted for a niche option that caters to a growing segment of Australia's population.

items.title: What governments need to do this time to avoid pre-NDIS mistakes
items.description: The states are once again on the hook for disability services due to the Commonwealth's drastic NDIS cuts. Can the mistakes of the past be avoided?

items.title: Trump is painting DC's reflecting pool. Here's why people are angry
items.description: Donald Trump has chosen a new colour for Washington DC's Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool. Here are three reasons it's proving to be controversial.

items.title: First home buyers 'up and about' at auctions after negative gearing changes
items.description: The government says the changes are aimed at levelling the playing field for young buyers bidding against property investors, while the opposition is pledging to undo the reforms, citing their potential to raise rents.

items.title: Rodrigues thought AI would make him rich. Then everything spiralled
items.description: Rodrigues thought an AI chatbot could help him escape poverty and build wealth. Instead, he became trapped in a spiral of delusion and dependence.

items.title: China quietly turns off supply of world's most used industrial chemical
items.description: Amid disruption from the Iran war, China has banned exports of sulphuric acid, a crucial component used to treat drinking water, refine petroleum and make batteries, clothing and phosphate fertilisers.

items.title: Taiwan remains committed to status quo after Trump's China trip
items.description: The Taiwanese government responds after US President Donald Trump's trip to China and his call for the two countries to "cool down".

items.title: 'You're malnourished; you are overtrained': Olympic gymnast's warning
items.description: Alexandra Kiroi-Bogatyreva trained up to 10 hours a day, six days a week, often without the proper nutrition. She wants others to know what that can do to the body.

items.title: Divers who faced jail for cultural fishing lead sea urchin recovery
items.description: After decades of fighting for their traditional fishing rights, Aboriginal custodians are now fighting to save their sea country from ecological collapse.

items.title: Top Hamas military leader killed in Israeli air strikes, official confirms
items.description: Izz al-Din al-Haddad is the most senior Hamas official to be killed by Israel since a US-backed ceasefire agreement meant to halt fighting was implemented in October.

items.title: Love, lust and the NDIS: what intimacy looks like with a disability
items.description: It's a stormy February night in Adelaide, and Jacqueline Tedmanson is at the hospital with her partner Jackson, waiting to meet their first baby.

items.title: Sam Kerr bids emotional Chelsea farewell with record-equalling goal
items.description: Sam Kerr ties the record for the most Women's Super League goals for Chelsea as she plays her final match with the London club after more than six years.

items.title: Caldwell becomes second-fastest Aussie with Diamond League podium
items.description: Abbey Caldwell beats four other Australians to third place in the women's 1,500m final on the first night of Diamond League racing for the year.

items.title: ‘His music is still alive’: Pride and sadness in posthumous Gurrumul honour
items.description: Nearly a decade since his death, Gurrumul is set to be inducted into the ARIA Hall of Fame, bringing pride and reflection to a remote part of Australia.

items.title: Rochelle Jordan's new album is so good, even she listens to it
items.description: The Canadian singer won widespread acclaim with her third album. Now she brings it to Australia.

items.title: Test your homophones and your Gen Alpha slang
items.description: Are you ready to test your spelling skills like your little lunch depends on it? Come on in.

items.title: Artist appointed, axed then reinstated from Venice Biennale triumphs
items.description: Last year, Khaled Sabsabi was appointed, sacked and then reinstated as Australia's representative to the Venice Biennale. Now he opens two installations at the world's most prestigious art exhibition.

items.title: 'Crisis situation': The Allan government is scrambling to remake donation laws
items.description: With only six months before the state election, the Victorian government struggles to devise new donation laws after the High Court found previous laws unconstitutional.

items.title: Gold Coast e-bike crackdown 'not effective', council report finds
items.description: A Gold Coast council report finds an e-bike crackdown has failed to significantly reduce anti-social behaviour, with many riders ignoring compliance officers.

items.title: Bushwalker takes photo of rare bug in the wild
items.description: There were no known photographs taken in the wild of the Myrmeleon houstoni until a regional Victorian woman snapped a photo of one while on a bushwalk.

items.title: Push to make rental properties ready for portable power future
items.description: A standard power plug for charging your home from an EV is among the measures proposed to improve energy standards for rental properties.

items.title: The darkness of a Tasmanian town's night sky could be protected
items.description: The northern Tasmanian town of Ross is working to protect its night sky, a years-long process that would see it formally recognised for its darkness and clarity.

items.title: Welcome to campdraft school, where a new generation takes the reins
items.description: Amid the red dirt and flies of an outback stockyard, thrillseekers with a passion for horses learn about a quintessential Aussie sport.
